dossier.purpose: Letta (formerly MemGPT) at 0.16.8 is, in this repository, a Python/FastAPI server plus REST API for stateful LLM agents with persistent, agent-editable memory (core memory blocks, archival passages, message history, optional git-backed memory repos), stored in PostgreSQL+pgvector through SQLAlchemy/Alembic. The README's headline CLI (Letta Code, npm @letta-ai/letta-code) lives in a separate repository that is not part of this revision; the `letta` console script defined here only launches the server.

claims.claim: Letta (formerly MemGPT): 'Build AI with advanced memory that can learn and self-improve over time.'
Two products are named: Letta Code ('run agents locally in your terminal') and the Letta API ('build agents into your applications').
The CLI requires Node.js 18+ and is installed with `npm install -g @letta-ai/letta-code`; the link points to a separate repo (github.com/letta-ai/letta-code).
'Run `letta` in your terminal to launch an agent with memory running on your local computer.'
'When running the CLI tool, your agent help you code and do any task you can do on your computer.' (sic)
Letta Code supports skills and subagents and 'bundles pre-built skills/subagents for advanced memory and continual learning'.
Letta is 'fully model-agnostic'; Opus 4.5 and GPT-5.2 are recommended; a model leaderboard (leaderboard.letta.com) is cited for rankings.
Letta has 'a full-featured agents API, and a Python and Typescript SDK'.
SDK installs: `npm install @letta-ai/letta-client` and `pip install letta-client`.
The Hello World example 'requires a Letta API key' from app.letta.com; agents are created with memory_blocks (human, persona) and tools web_search/fetch_webpage.
By using Letta and related services (such as the Letta endpoint or hosted service) users agree to the privacy policy and terms of service.

install.method: npm global (Letta Code CLI; separate repo; needs Node.js 18+)
From source with uv: self-hosted Letta server. Needs your own PostgreSQL with pgvector, LETTA_PG_URI exported, and the Alembic migration run by hand
install.command: uv sync --all-extras  (then)  uv run alembic upgrade head  (then)  uv run letta server

install.method: Docker Compose from the repo checkout (labelled WIP dev setup; compose.yaml itself uses image letta/letta:latest plus a pgvector database)

platforms.linux_x86_64: yes - Docker image is built for linux/amd64 (.github/workflows/docker-image.yml:34); CI runs on ubuntu-latest and self-hosted runners (e.g. .github/workflows/docker-integration-tests.yaml:11, reusable-test-workflow.yml:38); Python >=3.11,<3.14 (pyproject.toml:10). A native (non-Docker) run needs a local PostgreSQL+pgvector (CONTRIBUTING.md:30).
platforms.wsl2: unknown - no mention of WSL anywhere in the repo (searched); nothing documents or tests it.
platforms.macos_arm64: unknown - no explicit support statement and no macOS CI job (every workflow runner is ubuntu-latest or self-hosted). Indirect signs only: CONTRIBUTING.md:36-37 gives a 'Mac/Linux' Postgres step; uv.lock contains macosx arm64 wheel tags; the Docker image is also built for linux/arm64 (docker-image.yml:34). A native run still needs PostgreSQL+pgvector.
platforms.gpu: no - not required. The server has no local model inference: LLM/embedding calls are HTTP to providers or to user-run Ollama/vLLM/SGLang/LM Studio endpoints (letta/server/server.py:216-372; letta/settings.py:204-241; letta/local_llm/llamacpp/api.py only posts JSON to a server). Only the project's Ollama CI job asks for a GPU runner (.github/workflows/test-ollama.yml:38).

integrations.cli: Letta Code (npm @letta-ai/letta-code) is the README's CLI; it lives in a separate repo and cannot be read here (README.md:12-13). This repo's own console script `letta` (pyproject.toml:84-85 -> letta/main.py:5-16 -> letta/cli/cli.py:17-42) starts the REST server (`letta server`; options --host/--port/--debug/--reload/--secure/--localhttps; `--type websocket` raises NotImplementedError). Both packages use the command name `letta`.
integrations.mcp: No MCP server found in this repo. Letta acts as an MCP client: the /v1/mcp-servers router (letta/server/rest_api/routers/v1/mcp_servers.py:31-72) registers external MCP servers so agents can call their tools; stdio transport is disabled by default (letta/settings.py:45-54). The README does not mention MCP.
integrations.sdk_or_api: REST API (FastAPI), default port 8283, prefix /v1 (letta/server/constants.py:6; letta/constants.py:33; letta/server/rest_api/routers/v1/__init__.py:34-68); OpenAPI spec in fern/openapi.json. Memory-related routes: blocks (routers/v1/blocks.py:27-263), per-agent core-memory / archival-memory / messages / export / import (routers/v1/agents.py:295-531, 1206-1576), archives, conversations, passages search. Python `letta-client` and TypeScript `@letta-ai/letta-client` SDKs (README.md:26-34) are separate packages generated with Fern (.github/workflows/fern-sdk-python-publish.yml:34-44, fern-sdk-typescript-publish.yml:34-44); letta-client>=1.7.12 is also a dependency (pyproject.toml:46).
integrations.claude_code_or_codex: Claude Code: server-side proxy route POST /v1/anthropic/v1/messages (letta/server/rest_api/routers/v1/anthropic.py:32-50), excluded from OpenAPI (include_in_schema=False) and documented only in a docstring (set ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL in Claude Code settings.json). It appends the agent's memory blocks to the system prompt (proxy_helpers.py:260-330), forwards to https://api.anthropic.com (anthropic.py:28,135-137) and persists, per request, the last user message text plus the assistant text to an agent named claude-code-<first 8 chars of user id>, or the agent in the x-letta-agent-id header (anthropic.py:62-64,103-111; proxy_helpers.py:453-566; rest_api/utils.py:798-877). Tool calls/results are not captured; the Authorization header is not forwarded (proxy_helpers.py:125-136; API key comes from x-api-key / anthropic-api-key or the server's ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, 143-153). Codex: none found - no proxy, hook, skill, plugin or config for Codex (grep for 'codex' hits only model names and one comment at letta/services/summarizer/thresholds.py:37). No .claude/, SKILL.md, hooks or MCP config files ship in the tree, and no code reads or writes CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, ~/.claude or ~/.codex (.gitignore:8-9 merely ignores CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md). The README mentions neither Claude Code nor Codex.

readme.telemetry_and_network: README: only a legal notice that using hosted services implies accepting the privacy policy/ToS (README.md:122); its API examples need a Letta API key from app.letta.com (README.md:38). PRIVACY.md:6-8 says anonymous click/crash telemetry is collected and can be disabled with `telemetry_disabled = True` in a config file, but no such setting or analytics client exists in letta/ (searched telemetry_disabled, posthog, segment, mixpanel, amplitude); the YAML config only maps keys to env vars (letta/config_file.py:42-46,195-211). Outbound telemetry in code is opt-in: Sentry only if SENTRY_DSN is set (letta/server/rest_api/utils.py:46; app.py:300-308), Datadog only if LETTA_TELEMETRY_ENABLE_DATADOG (settings.py:538; app.py:310-408), OTLP only if LETTA_OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT (app.py:819-833). The Docker image runs an OTEL collector whose default config writes only to a local file (letta/server/startup.sh:79-91; otel/otel-collector-config-file.yaml:14-30); ClickHouse/Signoz exports need env credentials. Raw LLM request/response per step are stored in the local database by default (settings.py:382,387,571-574; services/telemetry_manager.py:21-33). Accounts/network: no Letta account is needed to run the server (default org/user created at startup: server.py:374-378; user_manager.py:113-135), but agent creation needs a model handle, so an LLM provider key or reachable local model endpoint is required (server.py:537-541). The Letta-hosted provider 'letta-free' (https://inference.letta.com/v1/ constants.py:8; https://embeddings.letta.com/ schemas/providers/letta.py:11) is always registered (server.py:216). Startup downloads NLTK punkt_tab data and only warns on failure (app.py:197-207). CORS allows https://app.letta.com and the startup banner links to the hosted ADE (app.py:795,915,954-957); the injected Claude Code memory prompt links to https://app.letta.com/agents/<id> (proxy_helpers.py:216-218); proxied Claude Code traffic goes to api.anthropic.com. Other optional outbound: step-complete webhook (WEBHOOK_SETUP.md:39-60) and Turbopuffer/Pinecone/E2B/Modal/Tavily/Exa/Mistral when keys are set (settings.py:22-31,425-446). Letta Code's own network behavior is not visible in this repo.

languages: Python (>=3.11,<3.14; .python-version 3.12; nearly all of letta/, tests/, alembic/)

entry_points.what: Typer app; the `server` subcommand is also what runs when no subcommand is given

Docker CMD: starts internal Redis/PostgreSQL unless LETTA_REDIS_HOST / LETTA_PG_URI are set, runs `alembic upgrade head`, starts the OTEL collector, then `letta server --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8283`

code.architecture: One FastAPI process (letta/server/rest_api/app.py) wires a SyncServer (letta/server/server.py) that owns 20+ service managers (letta/services/*_manager.py: agent, block, passage, archive, message, conversation, tool, mcp, provider, run, step, job, group, identity, ...). About 32 routers live in letta/server/rest_api/routers/v1/. Persistence: SQLAlchemy async ORM (letta/orm/, ~50 modules) over PostgreSQL+pgvector via asyncpg (letta/server/db.py), schema via Alembic; Redis is optional (letta/data_sources/redis_client.py falls back to a noop client). Agent loops are in letta/agents/ (agent_loop.py picks LettaAgentV3 for letta_v1_agent/sleeptime_agent, V2 for memgpt types); letta/groups/sleeptime_multi_agent_v3.py and _v4.py run a background memory-curation agent every N turns (default 5, server.py:784). Memory model: core memory blocks (letta/orm/block.py, letta/schemas/block.py; default 100000-char limit, constants.py:435) edited by the LLM through the `memory` tool (letta/functions/function_sets/base.py:10-68) plus core_memory_*, archival_memory_insert/search and conversation_search; archival passages/archives with optional embeddings (text-search fallback, tests/test_embedding_optional.py:1-6); messages in the DB. Optional git-backed memory (letta/services/block_manager_git.py; letta/services/memory_repo/: git CLI against repos kept under ~/.letta/memfs/repository/<org>/<agent>/repo.git by LocalStorageBackend, blocks stored as <label>.md with frontmatter) is enabled per agent by the `git-memory-enabled` tag and only when LETTA_MEMFS_SERVICE_URL is set (server.py:426-441). LLM clients for 15+ providers in letta/llm_api/ and provider schemas in letta/schemas/providers/. Tool execution: letta/services/tool_executor/ and letta/services/tool_sandbox/ (local subprocess by default; E2B or Modal if configured); MCP client in letta/services/mcp/. Observability: letta/otel/, letta/monitoring/, optional Sentry/Datadog. Background jobs: letta/jobs/ (APScheduler with leader election). Agent import/export (.af JSON) in letta/services/agent_serialization_manager.py and letta/schemas/agent_file.py. Also sandbox/ (Modal executor, TypeScript tool server), fern/ (OpenAPI spec), otel/ (collector configs).
code.packaging_and_release: Python package `letta` built with hatchling; the wheel target lists only the `letta` package (pyproject.toml:163-168), so alembic/, alembic.ini, sandbox/, otel/ and init.sql are not declared for the wheel (I did not build it to confirm). .github/workflows/poetry-publish.yml (named uv-publish): on GitHub release published or manual dispatch, `uv build` then `uv publish` with the PYPI_TOKEN secret (lines 2-33). .github/workflows/poetry-publish-nightly.yml: daily cron plus release/manual, renames the package to `letta-nightly` with a .devYYYYMMDDHHMMSS version (lines 2-8,45-64). .github/workflows/docker-image.yml: on release, builds linux/amd64+arm64 and pushes letta/letta and memgpt/letta tagged <version> and latest to Docker Hub (lines 3-40). SDKs are generated and published through Fern from fern/openapi.json (fern-sdk-python-publish.yml, fern-sdk-typescript-publish.yml; PYPI_TOKEN, NPM_TOKEN, FERN_TOKEN). No checksum, signature, SBOM, provenance-attestation or OIDC trusted-publishing step exists in any workflow (searched cosign/sigstore/attest/provenance/sbom/checksum/id-token); registry credentials are long-lived secrets. Build inputs are partly unpinned: uv installed with `curl ... | sh` (poetry-publish.yml:22-25), ghcr.io/astral-sh/uv:latest (Dockerfile:31), NodeSource `curl | bash` (Dockerfile:62), OTEL collector tarball downloaded without a checksum (Dockerfile:65-69); base image is pinned by tag and uv.lock is used with --frozen (Dockerfile:2,39). Release tags look like 0.16.8. Actual release assets and dates cannot be seen from this shallow clone.
code.tests_and_ci: pytest with pytest-asyncio (auto mode), pytest-order, pytest-mock, pytest-json-report (tests/pytest.ini; pyproject.toml:118-129,229-230). About 130 test modules: 93 tests/**/test_*.py (managers/ 21, mcp_tests/ 3, performance_tests/ 3, adapters/ 1, top-level ~65), 30 tests/integration_test_*.py, 5 tests/sdk/*_test.py, plus tests/mcp_test.py, tests/locust_test.py and 2 *_test.py inside letta/services/; 166 .py files under tests/ overall. Memory-relevant: tests/test_memory.py, tests/managers/test_block_manager.py (checkpoint/undo/redo at service level), test_passage_manager.py, test_archive_manager.py, tests/test_agent_serialization*.py, tests/test_embedding_optional.py, tests/test_git_http_post_push_sync.py and tests/integration_test_git_http_post_push_sync.py (its tests skip unless LETTA_MEMFS_SERVICE_URL is set, line 71). 31 workflow files in .github/workflows: core-unit-test.yml (23 pytest suites incl. managers/, sdk/, mcp_tests/ against pgvector:pg17 + Redis services), core-integration-tests.yml (8 integration suites), send-message-integration-tests.yml (5 provider configs), core-unit-sqlite-test.yaml, alembic-validation.yml and migration-test.yml (alembic upgrade head / check on Postgres and SQLite), docker-integration-tests.yaml (compose up, then tests/test_client.py), core-lint.yml (ruff check/format, semantic PR title; pyright runs with continue-on-error), test-pip-install.yml (pip install on 3.11-3.13, no tests run), model-sweep.yaml (manual provider/model scan), test-ollama/test-lmstudio/test-vllm, fern-check and fern-* preview/publish, issue-guard.yml (AI-policy issue gate), plus issue housekeeping. Test jobs run on self-hosted runners and inject vendor API-key secrets (reusable-test-workflow.yml:38,307-318,345-402) and reference a path absent from this tree (libs/config-core-deploy, line 336). Pre-commit has ruff, ty and trufflehog (.pre-commit-config.yaml).
code.dependencies: pyproject.toml: 69 direct core dependencies (lines 11-82) and 13 optional extras with 49 entries (lines 87-161): postgres 5, redis 1, pinecone 1, sqlite 2, experimental 2, server 3, bedrock 2, dev 10, cloud-tool-sandbox 1, modal 1, external-tools 6, desktop 14, profiling 1. fastapi and uvicorn==0.29.0 are declared only in the server/desktop extras (105-109,142-158); asyncpg only in the postgres extra (89-95) although letta/server/db.py needs it. Notable core entries: sentry-sdk[fastapi]==2.19.1 (38), opentelemetry-* exact pins (48-52), ddtrace/datadog (74,77), clickhouse-connect (78), temporalio (63), grpcio/grpcio-tools (41-42), llama-index (43-44), and black/ruff/ty as runtime dependencies (16,69,70). uv.lock (committed, revision 3, requires-python >=3.11,<3.14) resolves 344 packages; Docker installs with `uv sync --frozen --no-dev --all-extras` (Dockerfile:39). Node: sandbox/resources/server/package.json (2 dependencies: typescript, @types/node) with its lock file, and a stray root package-lock.json (name 'core') with no package.json.
code.security_policy: SECURITY.md: report by email to support@letta.com, not through public issues; acknowledgement within 48 hours and a fix/mitigation timeline within 7 days; security fixes are applied to the latest release only (SECURITY.md:3-14).

claim_checks.claim: Run `letta` in your terminal to launch an agent with memory running on your local computer, after `npm install -g @letta-ai/letta-code` (README.md:12-13).
claim_checks.evidence: Code differs from the README's wording for this repo: the CLI is in the separate letta-ai/letta-code repo, not in this tree. Here the `letta` console script (pyproject.toml:84-85 -> letta/main.py:5-16 -> letta/cli/cli.py:17-39) only launches the REST server, so two packages define the same command name. What the npm CLI stores, and whether it runs a local server or a hosted backend, cannot be read from this revision.

claim_checks.claim: Letta has a full-featured agents API, and a Python and Typescript SDK (README.md:22).
claim_checks.evidence: The API is real and broad: about 32 routers mounted under /v1 (letta/server/rest_api/routers/v1/__init__.py:34-68), with ~50 routes in agents.py alone. SDK source is not in this repo; the SDKs are generated by Fern from fern/openapi.json (.github/workflows/fern-sdk-python-publish.yml:34-44, fern-sdk-typescript-publish.yml:34-44); letta-client>=1.7.12 is a dependency (pyproject.toml:46).

SyncServer registers providers for OpenAI, Anthropic, Google AI/Vertex, Azure, Bedrock, Groq, Together, DeepSeek, xAI, MiniMax, Baseten, Z.ai, OpenRouter, Ollama, vLLM, SGLang and LM Studio from env settings (letta/server/server.py:216-372; letta/settings.py:132-241); agent creation needs an explicit model handle or LETTA_DEFAULT_LLM_HANDLE (server.py:537-541). Caveat: the auto-created Claude Code agent hard-codes anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929 and openai/text-embedding-ada-002 (proxy_helpers.py:548-552).

claim_checks.claim: Letta Code bundles pre-built skills/subagents for advanced memory and continual learning (README.md:17).
claim_checks.evidence: Skills and subagents belong to the separate letta-code repo. Only plumbing exists here: memory-repo paths skills/<name>/SKILL.md map to block label skills/<name> (letta/services/memory_repo/path_mapping.py:11-29) and agent files can carry SkillSchema entries (letta/schemas/agent_file.py:370-389); no SKILL.md files ship in this tree.

claim_checks.claim: Build AI with advanced memory that can learn and self-improve over time (README.md:3).
claim_checks.evidence: Memory mechanisms exist and persist in Postgres: core blocks edited by the LLM via the memory tool (letta/functions/function_sets/base.py:10-68), archival passages (base.py:164-243), and a background sleeptime agent that updates blocks every 5th turn by default (server.py:756-789; letta/groups/sleeptime_multi_agent_v4.py:131-168). Learning/self-improvement is not measured anywhere in the repo (no memory-quality eval found). Durability caveats: deletes of blocks, agents and passages are hard deletes (letta/services/block_manager.py:275-286; agent_manager.py:1334; passage_manager.py:778); block checkpoint/undo/redo exist only as service methods with no REST route (routers/v1/blocks.py:27-263) and no non-test caller (block_manager.py:842-1041).

claim_checks.claim: The Hello World example requires a Letta API key (README.md:38,45).
claim_checks.evidence: True for the hosted API. The self-hosted server needs no Letta key: it creates a default org/user (letta/server/server.py:374-378; letta/services/user_manager.py:113-135) and its only built-in auth is an optional shared password (app.py:797-799; middleware/check_password.py:23-27); repo tests point the SDK at a local base_url (tests/test_embedding_optional.py:35-43).

claim_checks.claim: PRIVACY.md (linked from README.md:122): anonymous telemetry is collected and can be disabled with `telemetry_disabled = True` in the config file (PRIVACY.md:6-8).
claim_checks.evidence: Code differs from the doc: `telemetry_disabled` appears only in PRIVACY.md; no analytics client or such setting exists in letta/ (searched telemetry_disabled, posthog, segment, mixpanel, amplitude), and the YAML config only maps keys to LETTA_*/provider/tool/DD_* env vars (letta/config_file.py:42-46,195-211). Outbound telemetry in code is opt-in only: Sentry (rest_api/utils.py:46; app.py:300-308), Datadog (app.py:310-408), OTLP (app.py:819-833).

claim_checks.claim: Claude Code can use Letta as a proxy by setting ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL (route docstring, not stated in the README).
claim_checks.evidence: The route exists and does inject memory and persist captures (letta/server/rest_api/routers/v1/anthropic.py:32-198; proxy_helpers.py:260-330; rest_api/utils.py:798-877). Limits seen in code: text only, last user message per request (anthropic.py:62-64; proxy_helpers.py:45-93); Authorization header not forwarded (proxy_helpers.py:125-136); the auto-created agent needs Anthropic and OpenAI providers (proxy_helpers.py:548-552) and a sleeptime agent is created only when an embedding config exists (server.py:757-759); route is hidden from OpenAPI (anthropic.py:32). I read the code only and did not run it.

claim_checks.claim: Opus 4.5 and GPT-5.2 are recommended; see the model leaderboard for rankings (README.md:17).
claim_checks.evidence: The leaderboard is an external site (leaderboard.letta.com) that was not fetched; no rankings exist in the repo. The only in-repo measurement is a provider/model compatibility scan dated 2025-06-20 (.github/scripts/model-sweep/supported-models.mdx:3,12).

risks: Scope/ownership: the README's headline CLI (Letta Code, npm @letta-ai/letta-code) is a separate repo outside this revision (README.md:12), so its storage, backend and Claude/Codex behavior are unverified here. This repo is the Python server/API; its `letta` console script starts a server (pyproject.toml:84-85; letta/cli/cli.py:17-39) while the README tells users to run `letta` for the npm CLI (README.md:13) - the same command name comes from two packages.

Integrations: no Codex integration of any kind was found (no proxy, hook, skill, plugin or config; grep for 'codex' hits only model names and one comment). The only Claude Code path is an undocumented, OpenAPI-hidden proxy that persists text only (last user message plus assistant text), skips tool calls/results, drops the Authorization header, and uses one agent per Letta user unless x-letta-agent-id is sent (letta/server/rest_api/routers/v1/anthropic.py:32,62-64,103-111; proxy_helpers.py:125-153,484-490; rest_api/utils.py:798-848). /v1/chat/completions chats with a Letta agent (model must be an agent id, streaming only), not with a model provider (routers/v1/chat_completions.py:62-66,112-116). No MCP server exists in the repo.

Memory is LLM-authored and token-costing: blocks are changed by the agent's memory tool (create/str_replace/insert/delete/rename, letta/functions/function_sets/base.py:10-68) and by a background sleeptime agent that reuses the main agent's model every 5th turn (server.py:770,784; groups/sleeptime_multi_agent_v4.py:144-145), created only when an embedding config exists (server.py:757-759). Memory units are free-text blocks with label/description/value/limit/metadata/read_only/tags/project_id (letta/schemas/block.py:13-44,77); no typed decision or handoff record was found. Org-wide message search needs Turbopuffer plus OpenAI embeddings and its route says 'cloud-only' (routers/v1/agents.py:2037; services/message_manager.py:1296-1303).

Deletion and recovery: deletes are hard (services/block_manager.py:275-286; agent_manager.py:1334; passage_manager.py:778); block history rows cascade-delete with the block (letta/orm/block_history.py:40-44) and normal update paths never write them (checkpoint_block_async has no non-test caller; no REST route for undo/redo); agent-file (.af) export has no archival passages or archives (letta/schemas/agent_file.py:431-445) and import recreates agents instead of restoring in place (routers/v1/agents.py:464-525). Git-backed memory history is opt-in per agent (git-memory-enabled tag), is constructed only when LETTA_MEMFS_SERVICE_URL is set, has service-only history readers, the /v1/git smart-HTTP route returns 501 without that URL and proxies to an external memfs service otherwise, and the cloud memfs_client.py is absent from this tree (server.py:426-441; services/block_manager_git.py:27,508-560; routers/v1/git_http.py:262-273; memory_repo/memfs_client_base.py:7-9). Requesting that tag without git memory configured strips the tag yet still prefixes block labels with system/ (server.py:602-645). No backup tooling exists in the repo.

Infrastructure weight: the server needs PostgreSQL with pgvector (CONTRIBUTING.md:30; settings.py:471-478 defaults to postgresql+pg8000://letta:letta@localhost:5432/letta; server/db.py:20-58 builds only an asyncpg engine). No code path creating a SQLite engine was found even though a `sqlite` extra, SQLite CI jobs and SQLITE branches exist (pyproject.toml:98; core-unit-sqlite-test.yaml; settings.py:491-493). The schema is created only by Alembic run by the operator (no create_all in letta/; CONTRIBUTING.md:75-79; Docker startup.sh:54-62) and the Alembic files sit outside the wheel's package list (pyproject.toml:167-168). The Docker image bundles Postgres 15, Redis, Node 22 and an OTEL collector in one container (Dockerfile:42-72). 69 core dependencies and 344 locked packages, with exact pins such as sentry-sdk==2.19.1 and uvicorn==0.29.0 (pyproject.toml:38,108; uv.lock). macOS arm64 and WSL2 have no explicit support statement.

Security defaults: no authentication unless --secure / LETTA_SERVER_SECURE adds one shared password, printed to stdout and compared by header equality (app.py:166-172,797-799; middleware/check_password.py:23-27); the acting user is chosen by a caller-supplied `user_id` header (routers dependencies.py:39,57-61). Docker startup binds REST to 0.0.0.0 and an internal Redis to 0.0.0.0 without auth (startup.sh:4,28,74); compose.yaml publishes Postgres on host port 5432 with default credentials letta/letta (compose.yaml:10-17). Agent-registered Python tools run as a subprocess of the server's own interpreter with the server's full environment, including provider API keys, unless E2B or Modal is configured (services/tool_sandbox/local_sandbox.py:114-145; base.py:487; settings.py:59-71). Provider/MCP secrets are stored in plaintext unless LETTA_ENCRYPTION_KEY is set (letta/schemas/secret.py:55-67). Stdio MCP is off by default (settings.py:45-54). SECURITY.md covers the latest release only (SECURITY.md:14).

Telemetry, network and legal notices: PRIVACY.md describes click/crash telemetry with an opt-out key that does not exist in code (PRIVACY.md:6-8). The code has no phone-home, but registers the Letta-hosted 'letta-free' provider by default, downloads NLTK data at startup, links to hosted app.letta.com (CORS, banner, injected Claude Code prompt), stores raw per-step LLM request/response (including injected memory) in the local DB by default, and logs captured-message previews at INFO in the proxy (server.py:216; app.py:197-207,795,915; proxy_helpers.py:216-218; settings.py:387; anthropic.py:159-166). README.md:122 and TERMS.md:4 tie use of 'Letta and related Letta services' to ToS/privacy acceptance and the repo does not say how that applies to self-hosted use; LICENSE is Apache-2.0 (LICENSE:176-180) while pyproject.toml:8 says only 'Apache License'.

Maintenance and process: this tree is an export of the apps/core directory of a monorepo (project.json:5; WEBHOOK_SETUP.md:183-194); every push to main notifies letta-ai/letta-cloud (.github/workflows/notify-on-update.yaml:17-29; letta-code-sync.yml:13-19) and CI references a path absent here (libs/config-core-deploy, reusable-test-workflow.yml:336) plus self-hosted runners and vendor API-key secrets (reusable-test-workflow.yml:38,307-318,359-399), so outside reproduction of CI is limited. Some docs are stale (WEBHOOK_SETUP.md:122 runs `python -m letta.server`, which has no __main__ module; letta/__init__.py:8 fallback version 0.16.7 vs 0.16.8). Schema churn is high: 167 Alembic revision files. Issues without AI-disclosure checkboxes and a verification phrase are auto-closed and locked (.github/workflows/issue-guard.yml:81-166; AI_POLICY.md:27-34). Releases carry no signatures, checksums or attestations and use long-lived registry tokens (see packaging_and_release).

checks.statement: Self-hosted server from source: needs your own PostgreSQL with pgvector, LETTA_PG_URI exported and the Alembic migration run by hand; `uv sync --all-extras` then `uv run alembic upgrade head` then `uv run letta server`.
checks.note: Every step is in the cited range: PostgreSQL plus the pgvector extension (CONTRIBUTING.md:30,57), `export LETTA_PG_URI` (61), `uv sync --all-extras` (72), `uv run alembic upgrade head` (78), `uv run letta server` (85). The code agrees. The only engine is asyncpg on settings.letta_pg_uri (letta/server/db.py:21,58), with default postgresql+pg8000://letta:letta@localhost:5432/letta (letta/settings.py:478). Alembic migrates Postgres only when a PG URI is set and otherwise writes a local SQLite file (alembic/env.py:17-26), so the export matters. `letta server` resolves through pyproject.toml:84-85 and letta/main.py:8. Side note, not a dossier error: CONTRIBUTING.md:112 wrongly says the database is set up automatically on first run.

LICENSE:1-176 is the standard Apache License 2.0 text. Lines 178-190 add 'Copyright 2023, Letta authors' and 'Licensed under the Apache License, Version 2.0'. It is the only license file in the tree (no NOTICE or COPYING; vendored dirs checked). pyproject.toml:8 says only 'Apache License' with no version, which the dossier already notes in its risks.

checks.statement: yes - Docker image built for linux/amd64; CI on ubuntu-latest and self-hosted runners; Python >=3.11,<3.14; a native run needs a local PostgreSQL+pgvector.
checks.note: Each citation checks out: `platforms: linux/amd64,linux/arm64` (docker-image.yml:34), `runs-on: ubuntu-latest` (docker-integration-tests.yaml:11), default runner `["self-hosted", "small"]` (reusable-test-workflow.yml:38), `requires-python = "<3.14,>=3.11"` (pyproject.toml:10), PostgreSQL required (CONTRIBUTING.md:30). No SQLite engine exists in letta/, so the Postgres requirement is real. The image build runs only on release or manual dispatch (docker-image.yml:3-6). The self-hosted runners' architecture cannot be seen from the repo.

Grep for 'codex' also hits a working `chatgpt_oauth` provider: it posts to https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex/responses using the 'Codex CLI / Letta Code' public OAuth client_id (letta/schemas/providers/chatgpt_oauth.py:1,23-29,106-136) with header 'OpenAI-Originator: codex' (letta/llm_api/chatgpt_oauth_client.py:89-169). It is wired in at enums.py:59, llm_client.py:132-135 and provider_manager.py:1063-1067. Grep also hits a 'codex-style' patch mode in the memory tool (function_sets/base.py:461; tool_executor/core_tool_executor.py:410,539) and a codex-cli comment (context_window_calculator/token_counter.py:90). (2) A second Claude Code proxy is omitted: POST /v1/zai/v1/messages, also hidden from the schema, forwards to https://api.z.ai/api/anthropic with the same inject/capture helpers (routers/v1/zai.py:9-50; mounted at routers/v1/__init__.py:32,36). (3) 'appends' is only half right: memory is appended when `system` is a list but prepended when it is a string (proxy_helpers.py:302-307).

checks.statement: partial: memory mechanisms exist (memory tool, archival passages, background sleeptime agent every 5th turn by default), but learning is not measured; deletes are hard; block checkpoint/undo/redo exist only as service methods with no REST route and no non-test caller.
checks.note: All citations match. The memory tool supports create/str_replace/insert/delete/rename (base.py:10-68), and archival insert/search are at base.py:164-243. The sleeptime group is created with sleeptime_agent_frequency=5 and is skipped when there is no embedding config (server.py:757-759,784); it runs every N turns (v4:140-168). Hard deletes are at block_manager.py:286, agent_manager.py:1334 and passage_manager.py:778. checkpoint/undo/redo are defined at block_manager.py:842/952/1004 and called only from tests/. The blocks routes (lines 27-263) have no such endpoint, and I found no memory-quality eval. Nuance: sleeptime is opt-in per agent (enable_sleeptime defaults to None, letta/schemas/agent.py:143-146); 'by default' applies only to the 5-turn frequency.
